children: Iron ore futures rose on Friday, clinching weekly gains, supported by destocking at major ports in top buyer China.
The most-traded January iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE)
closed daytime trade 0.91% higher at 723 yuan ($107.57) a metric ton. The contract gained 2.05% this week.
The benchmark September iron ore (SZZFU6) on the Singapore Exchange was 0.64% higher at $98.4 a ton, posting a weekly gain of 2.82%.
Iron ore inventory at major Chinese ports fell 1.03% week-on-week to 154.77 million tons, data from consultancy Steelhome showed.
Since the start of this month, shipments of low-grade ore have tightened and typhoon weather has also disrupted shipments, analysts from broker Yongsan Futures said in a note.
Mill profitability held steady at 32.47%, data from consultancy Mysteel showed.

The gradual recovery in steel mill profits is helping support hot metal output in August and September as the market shifts from the low-demand season to the peak-demand season, the Yongsan analysts said.
Iron ore supply is expected to increase in the fourth quarter and prices will be under pressure if domestic Chinese demand fails to recover meaningfully, they said.
Other steelmaking ingredients on the DCE rose, with coking coal
